_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS A MARKER IS A PAIR OF DELIMITERS AROUND A LIST — run it
from the repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- sweep \
crates/mnemosyne-cli/sweeps/inventory-marker.sweep.json
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. `inventory_markers = [{ open, close }]` declares the
delimiters an adopter writes around the inventory ids a document cites, and
everything between them is a whitespace-separated list of ids. Round 1322 read
a marker as a prefix followed by the section-path tail class, so it read the
first id of a list and never the rest, and cut an id at any character outside
that class; the adopter's own documents put two ids in one attribute on seven
of twenty-five annotated lines.
EIGHT INJECTIONS ON THE READER. A list that stops at its first id is the
Round 1322 defect; an id cut at a character class is its structural cause; an
unclosed marker dropped by the extractor or by the scan is the silence the new
axis exists to refuse; the one reader skipping the marker axis is how a caller
would miss it; and the longest-open, word-boundary and code-span rules each
have one test that asks them.
SIX INJECTIONS ON THE DECLARATION. Each refusal in `InventoryMarker::new` and
`InventoryMarkers::new` is turned off alone, and the marker's own
`deny_unknown_fields` is removed; each must redden the config test that asks
it, through the constructor and through a TOML declaration.
RUN IT LOCALLY. The harness edits this tree and writes the firing record
beside this file.

injections.name: a-list-stops-at-its-first-id
injections.why: the Round 1322 defect: the first id of a marker's list is read and every id after the first whitespace is not, so a deprecated or unregistered second id leaves the gate green

injections.name: an-id-ends-at-a-character-class
injections.why: the structural cause: the reader's alphabet is a borrowed character class instead of the store's id rule, so an id the store accepts is cut at a colon or a `#`

injections.name: an-unclosed-marker-is-skipped-by-the-extractor
injections.why: a marker whose close never follows read as citing nothing — indistinguishable from a document that cites nothing

injections.name: the-scan-drops-an-unclosed-marker
injections.why: the extractor returns the unclosed marker and the gate never turns it into a violation — the silence moved one layer up

injections.name: the-one-reader-skips-the-marker-axis
injections.why: the shape a caller that did not take the one reader would have: the axis is declared, parsed and echoed, and no citation under it is ever read

injections.name: the-longer-open-is-not-preferred
injections.why: two opens beginning at one place resolved by declaration order, so the shorter open reads the longer marker's delimiter into its ids

injections.name: an-open-may-continue-a-word
injections.why: an open beginning with a word character matched in the middle of a longer word, so `xreq="` cites as if it were `req="`

injections.name: an-example-in-a-code-span-is-read
injections.why: a marker quoted inside a backtick code span as an example is read as a citation

injections.name: an-empty-open-is-accepted
injections.why: an empty open begins a citation at every character

injections.name: a-line-break-in-an-open-is-accepted
injections.why: an open across lines has no line to open on, and the code-span rule is per line

injections.name: an-empty-close-is-accepted
injections.why: an empty close ends every list before its first id, so the marker reads as citing nothing

injections.name: whitespace-in-a-close-is-accepted
injections.why: whitespace separates the ids a marker encloses, so a close holding it would also end the list at a separator

injections.name: two-markers-may-open-alike
injections.why: which close ends a citation would depend on declaration order

injections.name: a-key-a-marker-does-not-model-is-dropped
injections.why: a declared key such as a separator the marker does not model would be accepted and silently ignored
